fields.meta_title: Sales Workflow Builder for Every Deal Stage | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Describe your stages and handoffs in plain English. Emergent builds the sales workflow that enforces them beside your CRM. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Sales Workflow From First Meeting to Kickoff
fields.hero_description: Build a sales workflow that keeps a deal out of the next stage until its fields are filled and hands each win to onboarding.
fields.features_heading: What Your Sales Workflow Can Enforce
fields.features_subheading: Each rule sits where a deal changes stage or changes hands, and every decision is logged against the deal it touched.
fields.feature_1:
Exit rules for each pipeline stage

Name the fields a deal needs before it can advance, like a confirmed budget for Proposal. A deal pushed ahead with one of them blank stays put, and its owner hears which field.
fields.feature_2:
SDR handoffs with an acceptance clock

Booking a first meeting requires a short handoff note. The account executive accepts it inside the window you set, or the meeting goes to the sales manager to hand to someone else.
fields.feature_3:
Discount approvals by percentage band

Reps approve their own discounts up to the limit you set. Larger ones go to the sales director in Slack, a second band adds the CFO, and the order form waits for the last yes.
fields.feature_4:
A closed-won record for onboarding

Marking a deal won opens an onboarding record that carries the contract value and every promise made during the sale. The onboarding manager who takes it is chosen by contract size.
fields.feature_5:
Days in stage on one dashboard

See how long each open deal has sat in its current stage, rep by rep. Handoffs nobody has accepted yet and discounts waiting on a director are pinned to the top of the board.
fields.feature_6:
Your sales rules as code you keep

Stage rules and approval bands export to your GitHub repository on paid plans as readable code. Each deal and approval is stored as a row in a database your team owns and can query.

fields.tab_content_1:
Missing budget and decision maker keep a deal in Discovery

Teodor Halbrook drags the $38,400 Linden Ridge Hotels deal from Discovery to Proposal. Proposal takes a deal only once its budget is confirmed and its decision maker is named. Both fields are blank. The deal stays in Discovery, and Teodor gets a Slack direct message naming them.
fields.tab_content_2:
The SDR's meeting waits 24 hours for an AE

Keziah Lisowski books a first meeting with the 240-person carrier Corriveau Freight and notes its pain point and buying timeline. Tobias Ardent, the regional account executive, is asked to accept. Accepting credits Keziah with the meeting. A handoff still unclaimed after 24 hours goes to the sales manager.
fields.tab_content_3:
22% off needs one more yes before the contract goes out

Anouk Severin offers Brambleton Dental Group 22% off a $52,000 annual plan. Reps can give up to 15% on their own. Anything above that goes to the sales director, and above 25% the CFO signs as well. Henrik Adair, the director, approves from Slack, and the order form goes out at $40,560.
fields.tab_content_4:
Once it closes, onboarding inherits every promise

Marking the Thistledown Veterinary deal closed won at $27,600 opens its onboarding record. The technical contact and a promised sync with the clinic's scheduling tool come with it. Contracts over $25,000 get a named onboarding manager. Yusra Thibault is assigned and holds the kickoff within five business days.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Sales Workflow
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to map the stages and handoffs of your sales workflow, set the rules for each, and build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down the stages you use
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write the stages in the order deals move through them, using the names your reps already say out loud. Next to each, note the one or two fields that must be filled before a deal leaves it, such as a signed order form before Closed Won.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Mark each point where a deal changes hands, such as SDR to account executive or account executive to onboarding. Name the giver and the receiver, and how long the receiver has to accept. A handoff with no owner is where a deal goes quiet.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give each discount band a percentage and a named approver: reps up to 15%, the sales director up to 25%, and the CFO above it. Add the exceptions too, like multi-year terms that always need finance. Plain sentences are enough to build from.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Describe all of it in one prompt. Emergent builds the handoff forms and approval steps around your rules, plus a board showing how long deals sit in each stage. When a rule changes next quarter, change it by prompting.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Connect the CRM your reps already work in, HubSpot or Salesforce for example, and deals sync in and out with their stage changes. Connect Slack for direct messages and approvals. Reps keep the screens they know while the rules run behind them.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Before launch, run last quarter's deals through the app. Check that each stage rule would have held the deals it should have and passed the rest, and that every discount reached the right approver. Correct any rule by prompting, then replay.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Turn it on for one team, such as mid-market, for a month. Watch handoff acceptance times and days in stage on the dashboard. Once the rules hold up, add the next team and retire the spreadsheet that used to track approvals.
fields.hero_prompt: Build a sales workflow for my team's deal stages, handoffs, and discount approvals.

plan.angle: The top 10 are glossary entries (DealHub, Clay), process explainers (ShareFile, PandaDoc, Highspot) and template galleries (n8n, OpsDog) that list stages and tools in general terms. This page shows the four points where a deal changes hands or needs a rule, built as one app beside the CRM: a stage that will not accept a deal with blank fields, an SDR handoff with a clock on it, a discount that climbs the approval ladder by percentage, and a closed deal that opens its onboarding record. Lead routing, follow-up sequences and renewals stay with the sales automation sibling and are linked.

A rep offers a dental group 22% off a $52,000 annual plan; anything over 15% needs the sales director, who approves in Slack, and the order form goes out at $40,560.

Marking a $27,600 veterinary deal closed won opens an onboarding record with the go-live target and what was promised in the sale; contracts over $25,000 get a named onboarding manager and a kickoff within five business days.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Sales Workflow From First Meeting to Kickoff', meta title 'Sales Workflow Builder for Every Deal Stage | Emergent', hero 'Build a sales workflow that keeps a deal out of the next stage until its fields are filled and hands each win to onboarding.' (123 chars); how-to description one sentence under 140 chars.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is glossaries, explainers and template galleries; FAQ 1 defines the term, FAQ 7 and 10 give examples and stages, the 7-step how-to and four worked tabs show the workflow built.

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary: 'Reps approve their own discounts up to the limit you set. Larger ones go to the sales director in Slack, a second band adds the CFO'; 'Replay last quarter's deals'.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: 'Teodor Halbrook drags the $38,400 Linden Ridge Hotels deal...', 'Name the fields a deal needs before it can advance...'.

craft.evidence: No tacked-on endings, no run-on lists; sentences vary: 'Both fields are blank.' / 'A handoff with no owner is where a deal goes quiet.'

voice.evidence: Reads as an operator wrote it: 'Set a time limit for each handoff so nothing sits unclaimed over a weekend.' No AI-tell vocabulary.

truth.evidence: faq item 8: 'In an app built with Emergent, each of those is one prompt, and the change history stays in your code.' states a platform behaviour (a retained change history) that is not in rules/capabilities.json; code-export covers GitHub export on paid plans only. All numbers agree: $52,000 less 22% = $40,560; $27,600 over $25,000; 22% between the 15% and 25% bands.

distinct.evidence: Stage exit rules, SDR-to-AE handoff, discount bands and closed-won handoff are distinct from sales-automation's lead routing, follow-up, stalled deals and renewals; QC D2 clean.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic items from the secondaries, answer-first, hub link in item 2, sibling links in items 4 and 7 (sales-automation, task-automation, both live), no brand or format in any question; PAA gate 6 pass, 0 reject, 4 flags (Divit's packet).

images.evidence: Contact sheet matches the copy: Linden Ridge Hotels $38,400 held with budget and buyer missing and a DM to Teodor; Corriveau Freight 240, Tobias Ardent, 24 hours; Brambleton $52,000, 22%, $40,560 net to Henrik Adair in Slack; Thistledown $27,600, over $25,000, Yusra Thibault, five business days.
